raw_response:
I'm 66, been working this land since I was 16. Never went to school, but I know these fields better than any book. My 14.5 mu, me and my old lady — just the two of us now, and we're not young anymore. Money's tight. We don't have much cash to throw around, so every yuan has to count. But I've also seen what happens when you cheap out on fertilizer: the wheat turns yellow and you regret it all winter. I'd rather spend a little more and sleep sound.

**Wheat this year:**

I plant wheat around October 10th, after National Day when the heat breaks. I save seed every year — been using the same kind for a long time, it's reliable. I buy a bit to top up what I don't have enough of, maybe 15 kg per mu. After the maize comes off, I plow the field and harrow it twice. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's 50 kg. I've always done it this way. My neighbor Wang tried less last year and his wheat was shorter than mine. Then in March or early April, when the wheat starts turning green after winter, I look at it. If it's a bit yellow, I spread half a bag of urea per mu, about 20 kg. If it looks good and dark green, maybe I do a little less, but usually I do the half bag. Better safe than sorry.

I irrigate three times: once before the ground freezes so the wheat can survive winter, once at jointing when it starts shooting up, and once at heading if it hasn't rained. Pumping costs money — the tube well is metered now — but dry wheat means no harvest. I spray herbicide once after the wheat comes up, and that's usually enough.

For harvest in early June, I hire a combine. Me and my old lady can't cut 14.5 mu by hand anymore.

**Maize this year:**

The wheat comes off around June 10th, and I have to get the maize in quick — usually within 3 or 4 days, otherwise the season gets too short. No time for deep plowing. I just do shallow rotary tillage and plant right away. I buy hybrid seed every year, about 2 kg per mu. You can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't work the second time. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow when I plant, about 40 kg per mu — a bit less than wheat because maize doesn't need as much to start. Then when the maize is knee-high, around mid-July, I spread about 15 kg of urea per mu. That's the critical time.

Summer rains usually help, but last couple years have been a bit dry. I plan to irrigate twice: once in July if the rain doesn't come, and once in August when the ears are filling. I put herbicide at planting, and if I see corn borer worms later, I spray insecticide. Most years I need to spray once for insects.

Harvest is late September or early October. Again, hired combine — the only way at our age.

**Money and labor:**

We're only two people, both over 65. Family labor is just me and my wife. We can handle the planting, fertilizing, and irrigating, but for harvest we must hire machinery. I watch every cost, but I won't cut fertilizer below what I know works. My target is about 400 kg/mu for wheat and 450 kg/mu for maize. If the weather is good, maybe a bit more. If it's bad, at least I won't have starved the crops.
